title: Tugboats: Pushing Their Way Around Since 1803
summary: Josh and Chuck (the transcript labels him iHeart Intro in places) research tugboats at listener Thomas's request, covering bollard pull and power-to-weight ratios, the Island Victory, tugboat design (beards, fenders), early history from Jonathan Hulls's 1737 patent and the 1801-1803 Charlotte Dundas era, the 1817 Dumbarton naming, Joseph Price's Tyne River colliers, paddle tugs and the Royal Navy's Comet and Monkey, the shift to screw propellers and diesel, the 1946 New York Harbor tugboat strike, electric and azimuth thruster tugs, fuel use, tug types (push, articulated tug barge, anchor handling, firefighting, icebreaking, salvage), crew roles and two-weeks-on schedules, and the Baltimore Key Bridge collapse and tug escort economics. The episode closes with a listener mail segment about the mysterious song "Subways of Your Mind" by Fix, identified via Reddit.
topics: Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse tug escort

segments.title: Opening and listener request
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the episode as a listener request from Thomas, who suggested tugboats after the Atlanta live show.

segments.title: Why tugboats are powerful and bollard pull
segments.summary: Hosts discuss tugboats' high power-to-tonnage ratio and define bollard pull, citing the Island Victory and typical harbor tugs measured in kilonewtons and tons.

segments.title: Tugboat design and maneuverability
segments.summary: Hosts describe the wide, low, stable build of tugboats, the front fender called a beard, tires used as bumpers, and their nimbleness for avoiding ships in shipping lanes.

segments.title: Need for tugboats and Jonathan Hulls
segments.summary: Sailing ships struggled in tight harbors and waited on wind. English inventor Jonathan Hulls patented a towing machine in 1737, which was mocked in a Gloucester song.

segments.title: Early steam tugs and canal towing
segments.summary: Hulls's invention was ignored for about sixty years before steam tugs were used in Scotland, where canal cargo had been pulled by donkeys along the shore.

segments.title: Charlotte Dundas and early Scottish towing
segments.summary: The paddle steamer Charlotte Dundas towed barges on the Forth and Clyde Canal near Glasgow, and steam tugs were also used on the Thames and in Liverpool.

segments.title: Origin of the name tugboat and Tyne River colliers
segments.summary: A 1817 Dumbarton steamship named Tug gave tugboats their name. In 1818 Joseph Price bought steam tugs to pull coal colliers on the Tyne River from Newcastle.

segments.title: Paddle tugs, Royal Navy, and diesel era
segments.summary: Early tugs used paddle wheels on both sides for maneuvering; the Royal Navy bought tugs Comet and Monkey; later screw propellers and diesel engines transformed tugs.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Ad break.

segments.title: 1946 New York Harbor tugboat strike
segments.summary: All roughly 300 New York Harbor tugboat operators struck in 1946, shutting down the city's barge-based supply, and the strike ended within twelve days.

segments.title: Fuel use, electric tugs, azimuth thrusters, and tractor tugs
segments.summary: Harbor tugs burn about 3,000 gallons of diesel daily; electric tugs like the Ewolf are emerging; azimuth thrusters rotate 360 degrees and tractor tugs use two independently controlled motors.

segments.title: Other tug jobs: salvage, search and rescue, firefighting, icebreaking
segments.summary: Tugs also handle salvage, search and rescue, and blocked canals such as the Ever Given case, with firefighting tugs and Navajo class search and rescue tugs mentioned.

segments.title: Anchor handling and line handling
segments.summary: Anchor handling tugs move massive oil rig anchors in the open ocean, and deckhands face danger from tensioned tow lines.

segments.title: Crew roles and work schedules
segments.summary: Crew includes engineers, mate, and captain. New York tug crews work two weeks on and two weeks off, with two six-hour shifts a day, which the hosts find grueling.

segments.title: Push boats and articulated tug barges
segments.summary: Push tugs use push knees against a barge's stern. Articulated tug barges pin a tug to a notched barge for oil shipping.

segments.title: Tug escorts and Key Bridge collapse
segments.summary: Tugs are contracted and historically raced to incoming ships. An AP article explains why the ship that hit the Francis Scott Key Bridge in Baltimore had no tug escort, citing cost and port competition.

segments.title: Wo Decker ride and tugboat appeal
segments.summary: Hosts mention riding the Wo Decker tug at South Street Seaport Museum in New York and discuss why people love tugboats.

segments.title: Beards, movie banter, and Dark Song
segments.summary: Banter about the word beard, Beetlejuice and Tim Burton films, and a recommendation of the horror film A Dark Song.

segments.title: Listener mail: Subways of Your Mind solved
segments.summary: A listener, Michael, reports that the mysterious song Subways of Your Mind has been identified as by the German band Fix from Kiel, via a Reddit user and a 1984 NordWest Zeitung article. Hosts say the band wants to re-record it.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts thank listeners, invite email at stuff podcast at iHeartRadio dot com, and close the episode.
